name: True Congenital Shoulder Dislocation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for True Congenital Shoulder Dislocation

criteria.description: Presence of shoulder deformity and limited passive and active range of motion at birth without history of trauma
Radiographic evidence of glenohumeral joint dislocation with absence of traumatic or obstetric injury
Exclusion of birth trauma or brachial plexus injury as cause of dislocation
Identification of associated musculoskeletal anomalies such as hypoplastic scapula or clavicle

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, radiological confirmation, and exclusion of trauma) must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; MRI may assist in complex cases

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital anterior or posterior glenohumeral joint dislocation
pathognomonic.notes: Dislocation present at birth without trauma
searchTerms: born with shoulder out of place

pathognomonic.symptomName: Limited passive and active shoulder joint mobility
pathognomonic.notes: Marked restriction of shoulder abduction and rotation
searchTerms: difficulty moving shoulder actively or passively

common.symptomName: Shoulder asymmetry with prominence of scapula
Muscle atrophy around the shoulder girdle
common.notes: Due to disuse or altered innervation
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk around shoulder

common.symptomName: Pain on passive movement in older infants
searchTerms: pain when moving arm in infants
reduced bone size in shoulder area
tingling or burning in upper arm nerves
grating or crackling sound in shoulder

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones related to upper limb

searchTerms: one limb shorter than the other
nerve damage affecting arm from birth

imaging: X-ray showing dislocation of humeral head from glenoid fossa
Ultrasound confirming absence of traumatic injury
MRI demonstrating soft tissue and joint capsule abnormalities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing fixed shoulder deformity
Electromyography to exclude brachial plexus injury

distinguishingFeatures: History of difficult delivery or trauma
Neurological deficits with sensory and motor impairment
Absence of true joint dislocation on imaging

redFlags: Signs of neurovascular compromise in affected limb
Severe pain unresponsive to conservative management
references: Bucholz RW, Heckman JD. Rockwood and Green's Fractures in Adults. 8th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2015.
